directAnswer: Pope Boniface III, a Roman of Greek descent, reigned for less than nine months in 607. A former envoy to Constantinople, he obtained from Emperor Phocas a recognition that the see of Rome was head of all the churches, and he held a synod regulating papal elections.

sections.h2: Envoy to the Court of Phocas
paras: Boniface was born in Rome to a family of Greek origin; the Liber Pontificalis names his father as John Cataadioce. Gregory the Great sent him to Constantinople as apocrisiarius, and there he gained the favor of Emperor Phocas. After Sabinian's death in February 606, almost a year passed before Boniface's consecration in February 607, a delay usually linked to waiting for imperial confirmation.

sections.h2: Rome as Head of All the Churches
paras: The Liber Pontificalis records that Boniface obtained a decree from Phocas declaring that the apostolic see of Peter was the head of all churches, in response to the patriarch of Constantinople's use of the title of ecumenical or universal bishop. The decree itself does not survive, and historians disagree about its exact wording and significance, but it reflects the long dispute begun under Pelagius II and Gregory I.

Boniface also held a synod in Rome attended by many bishops and clergy. It forbade anyone, under pain of excommunication, to discuss or arrange the election of a successor while a pope was still living, and it required that three days pass after a pope's burial before an election could take place. He died on 12 November 607 and was buried in St. Peter's. Little else about him is known.

keyFacts: Born in Rome to a family of Greek descent
Former papal envoy to Emperor Phocas
Obtained an imperial decree recognizing Rome as head of all churches
Synod banned electioneering for a successor during a pope's lifetime

faqs.question: What did Boniface III obtain from Emperor Phocas?
faqs.answer: According to the Liber Pontificalis, a decree stating that the see of Peter was head of all the churches. It answered the claims attached to the title of ecumenical patriarch used in Constantinople. The text of the decree has not survived.

faqs.question: What rules did Boniface III set for papal elections?
faqs.answer: His Roman synod prohibited discussing a pope's successor during his lifetime and ordered a waiting period of three days after a pope's burial before electing the next one.
